key_insight: APPLE introduces attribute-preserving pseudo-labeling to supervise diffusion-based face swapping, enabling accurate identity transfer while explicitly preserving target-specific attributes (pose, expression, lighting, skin tone, makeup).
problem_solved: Face swapping lacks real ground-truth, forcing a trade-off between identity transfer and preserving target attributes; diffusion-based conditional inpainting often degrades those target-specific attributes.
method: Generate pseudo ground-truth attribute labels from the target image (pose, expression, lighting, skin tone, makeup) to serve as conditioning signals.
Condition a diffusion-based inpainting/synthesis model on both source identity features and the target pseudo-attribute labels, with losses that enforce identity fidelity and attribute consistency.
Train end-to-end so the model learns to decouple identity from target attributes, producing high-fidelity swapped faces that retain target-specific appearance and geometry.
impact: Provides a practical way to supervise face swapping without real paired data, improving visual fidelity and attribute reliability. This benefits practitioners building realistic synthesis, data augmentation, and evaluation tools in face-related applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: source face + target face → pseudo-label extractor → conditioned diffusion inpainting → swapped output
Triplet comparison: source / target / swapped (side-by-side) to highlight identity transfer and attribute preservation
Attribute overlays: pose vectors, expression landmarks, and lighting/skin-tone maps showing preserved cues
Quantitative charts: identity similarity vs. attribute-preservation metrics and ablation bars showing effect of pseudo-labeling
paper_title: APPLE: Attribute-Preserving Pseudo-Labeling for Diffusion-Based Face Swapping
paper_authors: Jiwon Kang, Yeji Choi, JoungBin Lee, Wooseok Jang, Jinhyeok Choi
